correctness.rationale: For all k,r>=0, every complement of a selected (01)^k in (01)^(k+r) is a concatenation of r pairs 01 or 10 (prefix-balance parity); any maximal 10-block run consumes a distinct deleted 01 pair. Conversely inserting a 0 before and 1 after each 10-run produces a valid aligned alternating host, and extra deleted pairs may be appended. Counting j runs via 2j chosen block-boundaries gives binom(r+1,2j); saturation exactly r<=2k. Independently enumerated all deletion subsets in a bounded (k,r) grid and checked both binomial forms exactly. Unbounded claim is established by the constructive argument, not finite counts.
